claim: Whole-method human evidence is weak: about 30 positive industrial cases exist but come mostly from proponents and no controlled test shows staged design beats intuitive design.
agent_test: Not testable directly; treat staged prompts as unproven and always run an unstaged control at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Strict adherence to the staged method does not predict design quality; flexible followers do as well or better than strict followers.
agent_test: Compare a fixed S1-S9 order with a flexible order (agent may skip or reorder) at equal tokens on the same items.
audit_note: Supported, but the strict-worse results are secondhand (Fricke via Bender 2004, Rueckert via Motte's review) and the first Rueckert report found no correlation; Motte's own study is the same author as the review, so the evidence is one review plus one study.

claim: In a small observation of 4 of 21 designers (Pahl 1992, via Motte 2015), the two experienced designers got among the best results and the two inexperienced method-trained ones among the worst; the best result came from the experienced and method-educated designer, and the intuitive experienced designer was as good in half the time; the author concluded the method helps but cannot be separated from practical experience. One flexible student group with little experience failed until it followed the strict method (Rueckert et al.).
agent_test: Test a rigid scaffold on weak versus strong base models; expect gains mainly on weaker ones or novel tasks.
audit_note: In Pahl's 4-designer case the best result went to the experienced designer who was also method-educated, and the review concludes the method was 'all in all positive' but inseparable from experience; only one of the two experienced designers worked without the method, so 'experienced designers without method got top results' and 'experience beats method training' overreach an N=4 anecdote (the LLM papers d04/d14 listed as evidence are unrelated).
claim_before_audit: Experience beats method training: experienced designers without method got top results, method-trained novices got poor ones; one novice group needed the strict method first.

claim: Method gains are larger on new design than on variant (routine) design.
agent_test: Route easy items to a plain answer and hard items to staged flow; compare to staged on all.

claim: Early abstraction and separate function and effect search widens the set of solution principles found (worked example, not a trial).
agent_test: Add a function-abstraction step before generating; count distinct solution principles at equal tokens.

claim: Pahl's lever exercise: after abstraction, principle search and selection, material cost fell to 31 to 43 percent of the first solution (about 540 designers; first solution drawn by 90 percent).
agent_test: Measure whether a forced second pass after first idea improves a cost or quality score.

claim: A system-level morphological step improved design quality in a crossover trial of small teams (golf-ball 0.584 to 0.853, mouse 0.433 to 0.740), but n is 7 teams per group and Group A alone was not significant.
agent_test: Add a morphological table step (parts x options) and score combined concepts.

claim: Real design behaviour does not follow the Pahl and Beitz order: students raised structure issues early, while the model predicted late; requirements and function issues came early as predicted.
agent_test: Allow early solution sketches inside S1/S2 and compare to blocked ordering.

claim: Stage prompts have a perceived cost: a systematic method raised felt time pressure (d=.59) and effort (d=.29) and lowered motivation, with no gain in design rating (N=213).
agent_test: Log token and step cost of each stage; require each to earn its tokens.

claim: A prompted requirement-function-behaviour-structure chain raised human concept scores over free ChatGPT (3.31 vs 2.90 of 5, N=80), mostly in feasibility and usability for novices.
agent_test: Compare function-first prompt with free prompt on an LLM-only pipeline, with a code-based selector.

claim: A nine-role staged LLM pipeline lost requirements (coverage at most 20 percent) and was less often runnable than a two-agent loop, at 17 times the time; the simple loop's high runnability partly came from collapsing to one node. A manual audit (d01) traced much of the low coverage to empty linked_reqs fields and drifting requirement IDs counted as misses by an exact-match checker, so some of the loss is bookkeeping, not lost content.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison of a staged pipeline and a generate-and-reflect loop with a requirement-coverage checker.

claim: Staged role pipelines (waterfall) beat single-step LLM code generation: ChatDev quality 0.3953 vs 0.1523 and 0.1419, executability 0.88 vs 0.41 and 0.36.
agent_test: Run staged vs single-step on code tasks at equal tokens; ChatDev did not control for token use.

claim: Multi-agent staged LLM systems fail often (41 to 86.7 percent) and mostly from specification, inter-agent misalignment and weak verification; better role prompts gave +9.4 points and a verification loop +15.6 on ChatDev.
agent_test: Add a code-checked verification step at stage ends; measure the gain over more stages.

claim: In one early-stage test, GPT-4o functional decompositions were rated about as complete as those of 12 student groups (3.96 vs 3.91; lower on creativity, 3.12 vs 3.48); separately, a fine-tuned 7B model (ReqGPT) beat GPT-4 on requirements lists in rater similarity scores (77% vs 69%), without a student comparison.
agent_test: Test the agent's S1 requirement list against rubric criteria with and without a clarify step.
audit_note: Only the functional-decomposition study (12 student groups, GPT-4o lower on creativity) compares with students; the ReqGPT 77% vs 69% result is LLM vs LLM with no student baseline, so 'individual early stages about as well as students' is wider than the sources.
claim_before_audit: LLMs do individual early stages about as well as students: functional decomposition completeness 3.96 vs 3.91; a fine-tuned 7B beat GPT-4 on requirements lists (77% vs 69%).

claim: In one 2023 study with GPT-3 (Ma et al.), LLM concepts were rated more feasible and useful but less novel than crowdsourced ones; GPT-3 repeated itself after a few outputs, adding a 'unique' adjective gave the smallest convex-hull volume (0.186) and few-shot examples also lowered coverage (0.2) versus 0.294 for the crowd; a separate small chair-design study found a lower share of unique terms for ChatGPT (67.4%) than for human designs (78.2%).
agent_test: Measure distinct-concept count with and without a forced-alternatives step.
audit_note: Repetition, feasible-but-less-novel, unique-adjective and few-shot results all come from one GPT-3 study (Ma et al. 2023, listed three times); the other cited sources (Egea: ChatGPT team placed 2nd; Chen: unique-term share) do not show repetitiveness, so 'a plain LLM' and independence are overstated.
claim_before_audit: A plain LLM gives feasible but unoriginal and repetitive concepts; novelty wording did not fix it and few-shot examples shrank diversity.

claim: An LLM running TRIZ steps matched textbook contradictions in 7 of 10 cases within the top 3 detections; entropy over repeats flagged low-agreement cases.
agent_test: Use repeat-run agreement on an S2 decision as a confidence signal.

claim: An LLM that dropped a promising concept at a small hitch and fixated on details lost to the best human team (14.8 m vs 37 m) in a hackathon; one case.
agent_test: Test a persistence rule: keep a rejected concept alive until a check fails twice.

claim: Agentic engineering pipelines are judged reliable only with repeats: 10 of 10 passes is below 29 consecutive passes needed for 90 percent reliability at 95 percent confidence.
agent_test: Report pass^k not single-run pass on every staged arm.

claim: No published LLM study runs the full Pahl and Beitz or VDI 2221 sequence against a plain model at equal tokens.
agent_test: This is the open experiment for our agent.

claim: VDI 2221 lost its thinking advice and decision checks relative to VDI 2222, which authors link to weak practitioner uptake.
agent_test: Keep checks at stage ends (decision: go on or repeat) rather than bare instructions.

claim: Added reasoning structure pays mainly on formal, verifiable tasks: CoT gains average 14.2 (symbolic), 12.3 (math), 6.9 (logic) points, but only 0.7 points elsewhere (56.8 vs 56.1); up to 95% of the MMLU gain came from equals-sign questions.
agent_test: Route open-ended generation to a light flow and formal checks (constraints, arithmetic, code) to staged steps; compare with always-staged at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The gain from added structure shrinks with model strength on reasoning-type prompts (Llama 8B > GPT-3.5 > GPT-4o-mini for structured representations; CoT negligible for o3-mini, o4-mini, Flash 2.5), but a rich task-method-knowledge prompt lifted o1 on a formal planning task (random Blocksworld 31.5% to 97.3%). Strength-dependence is task-dependent.
agent_test: Run the scaffold and a plain arm on one weak and one strong model on the same items; report the gain for each, and the token ratio.

claim: Letting the model choose and adapt its own reasoning structure beat fixed CoT and plan-and-solve (GPT-4 BBH 81 vs 75 and 73; T4D 85 vs 52 and 53) at one call per instance. Order flexibility inside one problem was not tested.
agent_test: Compare agent-selected stage subset and order against fixed S1-S9 on the same items at equal tokens.

claim: Stage cost is real: CoT-style steps added 35-600% time for non-reasoning models and 20-80% for reasoning models, and cut strict 25/25 reliability on several models.
agent_test: Give each stage a token cap and keep it only if it beats the plain arm at that cost.

claim: A code-based requirements ledger (fixed IDs, per-node link check) is the plausible fix for requirement loss in staged pipelines; no study has tested it.
agent_test: Add a ledger arm with code that lists unmet requirement IDs after each stage; measure coverage against a no-ledger arm.

claim: GPT-4o shows design fixation in a small study (unique-term share 67.4% vs 78.2% for human award entries, N=10), and professionals anchor on an LLM's first design; no frontier replication of Egea's concept abandonment or test of a persistence rule exists.
agent_test: Force 3 distinct concepts before choosing; keep a rejected concept alive until a check fails twice; count distinct concepts.
